title: Photo-induced Wavelength-tuning of Telecom-band Quantum Dot Nanowires Embedded in a Phase Change Material
authors: Evangelos Sotiropoulos, Philippe Regreny, Matthieu Bugnet, Nicholas P. Blanchard, Sébastien Cueff, José Penuelas, Nicolas Chauvin
abstract: Scalable quantum-photonic technologies require spatially separated emitters to emit at the same wavelength, yet epitaxially grown quantum dots naturally exhibit emitter-to-emitter variations in their emission energies. Here, we demonstrate a contact-free post-growth tuning approach for InAs quantum dots embedded in InP nanowires using the photo-induced transformation of an amorphous Sb2S3 shell. This photoinduced effect leads to a progressive relaxation of the strain imposed on the InP core, enabling controlled spectral tuning of the quantum-dot emission. The effect is observed both at room temperature and under cryogenic conditions for quantum dots emitting in the O-band of the telecommunications spectrum. Strain-induced redshifts of approximately 7 meV at room temperature and 28 meV under cryogenic conditions are observed, respectively. The use of an amorphous chalcogenide shell therefore provides a route to achieve local wavelength tuning at the single quantum-dot-in-a-nanowire level after growth. This approach could enable spectrally matched emitters for scalable quantum-photonic architectures.
summary: This research presents a novel, contact-free method to tune the emission wavelength of quantum dots embedded in nanowires by utilizing a photo-induced strain relaxation mechanism in an overlying amorphous shell. By controlling the local strain environment, the authors achieve significant, persistent spectral shifts, enabling the creation of spectrally matched emitters for quantum photonic applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving spectrally matched emitters for scalable quantum-photonic technologies, due to inherent emitter-to-emitter variations in quantum dot emission energies.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a contact-free, post-growth spectral tuning of quantum dot emission by inducing a photo-driven relaxation of strain within the surrounding amorphous chalcogenide shell.
method: The tuning is achieved by exposing the InAs quantum dot nanowires, coated with amorphous Sb2S3, to specific wavelengths of laser light, which modifies the local strain environment.
model_or_system: The system consists of InAs quantum dots embedded in InP nanowires, which are coated with an amorphous Sb2S3 shell. The tuning mechanism is attributed to the photo-induced transformation of the amorphous shell, leading to progressive strain relaxation on the InP core.
key_observables: Spectral redshift of the QD emission energy ($\sim 7 	ext{ meV}$ at RT; $\sim 28 	ext{ meV}$ at 12 K); lattice parameters and strain components derived from XRD; optical contrast changes upon laser irradiation.
important_parameters: Temperature (Room Temperature vs. 12 K); Laser wavelengths (532 nm vs. 671 nm); Strain magnitude ($	ext{meV}$ shifts).
main_assumptions: The observed redshift is primarily due to strain relaxation caused by the photo-induced structural change in the amorphous shell, rather than simple heating or crystallization.
figures_summary: Figures show $\mu$-PL spectra demonstrating persistent redshifts after laser exposure, and STEM/XRD data are used to quantify the strain changes induced by the shell deposition and subsequent photo-treatment.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for spectral matching to detailing the photo-induced tuning effect, quantifying the redshift at different temperatures, and finally elucidating the mechanism by comparing different laser wavelengths and observing structural changes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it presents a robust, external method to engineer the energy levels (emission wavelength) of solid-state emitters post-fabrication, which is crucial for building integrated quantum circuits.
